kevin-platform: quick q — when we mark v1 as deprecated but v2 still has opt-in features, what should default routing do? sticky per-customer or honor client headers + console override?

sarah-eng: +1 for sticky-by-customer for stability. header should trump only if explicit 'force' set. sticky gives predictable UX during slow rollouts. we need a grace accounting window tho (clients hitting both models).

lucas-ops: we hit a huge quota spike last time when auto-switched thousands of keys. propose quota-smoothing + temporary burst pool. moving-average smoothing (1h) + credit pool to absorb initial spikes.

jordan-pm: for console UX: add a "compatibility mode" toggle at project level (off by default). show expected token delta and a small rollout slider (canary %). admins can force v1 if needed.

maria-analytics: we can estimate token delta by sampling top-5k keys. I'll run a token-ratio job (v2_tokens / v1_tokens) and produce a per-project estimate for the console to display.

anya-devex: UX suggestion — two controls: "Preview v2" (preview only your requests) and "Canary rollout" (percent slider). show a red/yellow/green signal from telemetry: latency/regression/quality. keep toggle discoverable.

sarah-eng: routing pseudocode for negotiation (rough):
```
# headers from client
X-Client-Version: 1.0
X-Prefer-Version: v2
X-Routing-Override: force-v1

# server routing logic
if X-Routing-Override == 'force-v1':
    route(v1)
elif sticky_map[customer_id] exists and not expired:
    route(sticky_map[customer_id])
elif X-Prefer-Version == 'v2' and policy.allows_header_preference:
    route(v2)
else:
    route(policy.pick_for_customer(customer_id))
```
We should also set sticky_map TTL and store the reason (canary/override).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolled v2-slim to dedicated pool at 2026-03-10T03:12:00Z :white_check_mark:

kevin-platform: big open concern — token accounting fairness. v2 tokenization and model compression mean "tokens" don't map cleanly to cost. If we auto-switch customers, they'll suddenly burn more/less quota. Do we normalize quotas or present projected delta?

lucas-ops: solution: maintain a per-model multiplier (model_token_weight). normalized_units = raw_tokens * model_token_weight. during migration we can set multipliers so customers see smooth billing. store multiplier on billing / quota side and expose estimates in console.

maria-analytics: I'll add an "estimated_token_ratio" telemetry field to our migration samples: {model, sample_key, tokens_v1, tokens_v2, ratio}. will run across three weeks of traffic.

jordan-pm: rollout plan proposal: 5% canary -> 25% over 2 weeks -> 100% over 1 month unless regressions. Alert if latency increases > 15% or eval-quality drop > 2% on golden prompt set. Also auto-rollback trigger if error-rate spike > 3x baseline.

anya-devex: one more question: should console block "switch to v2" if project has active compliance flags (SSO/data residency) that require private deployment? maybe show a warning and require admin confirmation.

sarah-eng: I'll prototype the middleware today. proposed config knobs: fallback_timeout_ms, sticky_ttl_days, header_preference_enabled, quota_multiplier_map. will push a PR and tag ppl who want to test. :rocket:
